# rk8s

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/ian-flores/rk8s/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ian-flores/rk8s/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

A Kubernetes client for R.

``` r

library(rk8s)
k <- kube()
kube_get(k, "pods")
```

rk8s reads your kubeconfig the way kubectl does, so if
`kubectl get pods` works, so does the code above.

Most of the time you’ll use a handful of verbs:
[`kube_get()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_get.md),
[`kube_apply()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_apply.md),
[`kube_logs()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_logs.md),
[`kube_scale()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_scale.md),
[`kube_watch()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_watch.md)
and
[`kube_delete()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_delete.md).
They take manifests as YAML or plain R lists. Behind them is a client
generated from the Kubernetes OpenAPI spec (`CoreV1Api`, `V1Pod` and so
on, 944 operations in all) for anything the verbs don’t cover.

There’s also what you need to run a controller in R: watches, an
informer cache, and leader election on a Lease.

## Installation

rk8s isn’t on CRAN yet. Install it from GitHub:

``` r

remotes::install_github("ian-flores/rk8s")
```

For
[`pod_exec()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/pod_exec.md)
and
[`pod_port_forward()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/pod_port_forward.md)
you also need `nanonext`, and for leader election `callr`.

## Usage

[`kube()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/Kube.md) uses
`$KUBECONFIG` (or `~/.kube/config`) and the current context. Its
`context`, `config_file` and `namespace` arguments change that.

``` r

k <- kube()

kube_apply(k, "
  apiVersion: apps/v1
  kind: Deployment
  metadata: {name: nginx}
  spec:
    replicas: 3
    selector: {matchLabels: {app: nginx}}
    template:
      metadata: {labels: {app: nginx}}
      spec:
        containers: [{name: nginx, image: nginx:1.25}]
")

kube_get(k, "deployment/nginx")
as.data.frame(kube_get(k, "pods"))

kube_scale(k, "deployment", "nginx", replicas = 5)
cat(kube_logs(k, "nginx-abc", tail = 50))
kube_delete(k, "deployment/nginx")
```

[`kube_apply()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_apply.md)
does a server-side apply, and also takes a file path or an R list:

``` r

kube_apply(k, "deployment.yaml")
kube_apply(k, list(
  apiVersion = "v1", kind = "ConfigMap",
  metadata = list(name = "demo"),
  data = list(hello = "world")
))
```

You can name a resource as `"pods"`, `"pod"`, `"po"`,
`"deployment/nginx"`, `"apps/v1:Deployment"` or
`c("apps/v1", "Deployment")`. Custom resources work the same way; rk8s
looks up where they live through API discovery.

### Watching

``` r

kube_watch(k, "pods", timeout_seconds = 30, on_event = function(type, obj) {
  message(type, " ", obj$metadata$name)
  TRUE   # return FALSE to stop
})
```

For a controller you usually want an informer instead. It lists once,
keeps a local copy up to date from a watch, and calls your handlers:

``` r

inf <- Informer$new(k$client,
  resource_path = "/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods",
  object_from_list = V1Pod$from_list)

inf$add_event_handler(
  on_add    = function(obj) message("add: ", obj$metadata$name),
  on_update = function(old, new) message("update: ", new$metadata$name),
  on_delete = function(obj) message("delete: ", obj$metadata$name))

inf$run(stop_seconds = 120)
inf$lister()$get("nginx", namespace = "default")
```

### Leader election

If you run several copies of a controller, only one should act at a
time:

``` r

run_as_leader(k$client,
  lease_name = "my-controller",
  lease_namespace = "kube-system",
  identity = paste0(Sys.info()[["nodename"]], "-", Sys.getpid()),
  on_started_leading = function(leader) {
    repeat {
      leader$check()
      reconcile_once()
      Sys.sleep(5)
    }
  },
  on_stopped_leading = function() message("stopped"))
```

A background process keeps renewing the lease. `leader$check()` throws
as soon as the lease is lost, which ends your loop before another
replica takes over, so call it often.

### Exec and port-forward

``` r

r <- pod_exec(k$client, "default", "nginx-abc", c("ls", "/"))
cat(r$stdout)
r$exit_code

fwd <- pod_port_forward(k$client, "default", "nginx-abc", remote_port = 80)
httr2::req_perform(httr2::request(paste0("http://127.0.0.1:", fwd$port)))
fwd$close()
```

These run over a WebSocket, which has to authenticate with a token. The
default users that kind, minikube and kubeadm create only have a client
certificate, so with those you’ll need a ServiceAccount token:

``` r

# kubectl create serviceaccount rk8s-dev
# kubectl create clusterrolebinding rk8s-dev --clusterrole=edit \
#   --serviceaccount=default:rk8s-dev
cfg <- load_kube_config()
cfg$api_key <- list(authorization = paste(
  "Bearer", system("kubectl create token rk8s-dev", intern = TRUE)))
k <- kube(client = ApiClient$new(cfg))
```

### The generated API

When the verbs don’t have what you need, use the generated classes
directly. Their method names match the official Python client.

``` r

core <- CoreV1Api$new(k$client)
pods <- V1PodList$from_list(core$list_pod_for_all_namespaces())

dep <- V1Deployment$new(
  api_version = "apps/v1", kind = "Deployment",
  metadata = V1ObjectMeta$new(name = "nginx"),
  spec = V1DeploymentSpec$new(
    replicas = 3L,
    selector = V1LabelSelector$new(match_labels = list(app = "nginx")),
    template = V1PodTemplateSpec$new(
      metadata = V1ObjectMeta$new(labels = list(app = "nginx")),
      spec = V1PodSpec$new(containers = list(
        V1Container$new(name = "nginx", image = "nginx:1.25"))))))

AppsV1Api$new(k$client)$create_namespaced_deployment(
  namespace = "default", body = dep)
```

## Authentication

rk8s supports what’s commonly found in kubeconfig files: tokens and
token files, client certificates, basic auth, exec plugins (EKS, GKE,
kubelogin and others), the `oidc` auth-provider, `proxy-url`,
`tls-server-name`, `insecure-skip-tls-verify`, and a `KUBECONFIG` that
lists several files. Inside a pod, use the ServiceAccount instead:

``` r

k <- kube(client = ApiClient$new(load_incluster_config()))
```

## Development

The classes in `R/gen_*.R` are generated from the OpenAPI spec pinned in
`tools/gen/spec/`. To target a newer Kubernetes release, replace the
spec and regenerate:

``` bash
Rscript tools/gen/generate.R tools/gen/spec/swagger.json R
```

The unit tests run against fake API servers. The integration tests in
`tests/integration/` need a cluster you don’t mind writing to (kind
works):

``` bash
RK8S_E2E=1 Rscript tests/integration/run.R
```

# Package index

## Sessions and verbs

Start with
[`kube()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/Kube.md). The
verbs cover everyday work without touching the generated classes.

- [`kube()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/Kube.md) : Open
  a Kubernetes session
- [`kube_get()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_get.md)
  : Get one or many Kubernetes resources
- [`kube_list()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_list.md)
  : List a resource (always; never returns a single object)
- [`kube_apply()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_apply.md)
  : Server-side apply a manifest
- [`kube_delete()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_delete.md)
  : Delete a resource
- [`kube_scale()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_scale.md)
  : Scale a workload (Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet,
  ReplicationController)
- [`kube_logs()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_logs.md)
  : Stream pod logs
- [`kube_watch()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/kube_watch.md)
  : Watch a resource

## Connecting and authenticating

- [`load_kube_config()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/load_kube_config.md)
  : Load configuration from a kubeconfig file
- [`load_incluster_config()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/load_incluster_config.md)
  : Load configuration from the in-cluster service account
- [`list_kube_config_contexts()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/list_kube_config_contexts.md)
  : List contexts in a kubeconfig
- [`new_client_from_config()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/new_client_from_config.md)
  : Shorthand for loading config + constructing an ApiClient.
- [`Configuration`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/Configuration.md)
  : Kubernetes client configuration
- [`ApiClient`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/ApiClient.md)
  : Kubernetes API client
- [`ApiException`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/ApiException.md)
  : Kubernetes API exception

## Watches and caches

Building blocks for controllers.

- [`Watch`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/Watch.md) :
  Watch a Kubernetes list endpoint
- [`Informer`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/Informer.md)
  : Shared Informer - local cache of a resource, kept in sync via watch
- [`Lister`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/Lister.md) :
  Read-only indexed view over an Informer's cache
- [`WorkQueue`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/WorkQueue.md)
  : Work queue for controllers
- [`run_as_leader()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/run_as_leader.md)
  : Run as the leader under a Kubernetes Lease

## Controllers and operators

Run reconcile loops in R: informers feed a work queue, and your
reconcile function makes the cluster match each object.

- [`Manager`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/Manager.md) :
  Run controllers: informers, a work queue and a reconcile function
- [`requeue()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/requeue.md)
  [`requeue_after()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/requeue.md)
  : Reconcile results

## Exec and port-forward

WebSocket sessions to pods. Need the `nanonext` package and a bearer
token; the API server’s certificate is always verified unless the
kubeconfig says `insecure-skip-tls-verify`.

- [`pod_exec()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/pod_exec.md)
  : Run a command in a pod, capture stdout/stderr/exit code
- [`pod_exec_open()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/pod_exec_open.md)
  : Open an interactive exec session on a pod
- [`PodExecSession`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/PodExecSession.md)
  : Pod exec session
- [`pod_port_forward()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/pod_port_forward.md)
  : Forward a pod port to a local TCP listener (kubectl-style)
- [`pod_port_forward_open()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/pod_port_forward_open.md)
  : Open a port-forward session to a pod
- [`PodPortForwardSession`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/PodPortForwardSession.md)
  : Pod port-forward session

## Custom resources and discovery

- [`DynamicClient`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/DynamicClient.md)
  : Dynamic (untyped) Kubernetes client
- [`create_from_yaml()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/create_from_yaml.md)
  : Create one or more Kubernetes resources from a YAML manifest
- [`parse_quantity()`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/parse_quantity.md)
  : Parse a Kubernetes resource quantity
- [`rk8s`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/rk8s-package.md)
  [`rk8s-package`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/rk8s-package.md)
  : rk8s: Kubernetes client for R

## Models

R6 model classes for every Kubernetes object, generated from the OpenAPI
spec. Each has `$new()`, `$to_list()` and `$from_list()`.

- [`V1APIGroup`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/V1APIGroup.md)
  : V1APIGroup
- [`V1APIGroupList`](https://ian-flores.github.io/rk8s/reference/V1APIGroupList.md)
  : V1APIGroupList

  : V1APIResource

  : V1APIResourceList
